what: The WolframCloud MCP server entry, removed from the desktop application config.
why: It retried a failing endpoint every few minutes and raised an alert each time. The founder instructed the edit on 2026-09-10: 'Edit the file to stop the alerts then continue with the remaining work. I'm not at home so I can't do it.'
not_a_deletion: The entry is preserved verbatim below and the whole config is backed up at the path named in `backup`. Restoring is one paste. This matters because task W1 is the founder asking Wolfram whether the MCP licence can be renewed, and he said of the route: 'It has its uses.'
measured: scripts/wolfram_route_health_2026-09-10.py: 43 failures of 64 connection attempts, 67.1875%, Wilson 95% [54.9991%, 77.4294%] agreeing between statsmodels and mpmath to 1e-9, Clopper-Pearson [54.3123%, 78.4128%].
not_dead: WITHDRAWN AS WRITTEN, 15 minutes after writing it. The first version of this field said '21 of 64 attempts SUCCEEDED and the most recent success was 2026-09-09, so the route is unreliable, not dead'. Every number in that sentence is true and the sentence is still misleading, because it pools across a change point. Before 2026-09-04, 1 of 21 attempts failed (4.7619%). From 2026-09-04, 42 of 43 failed (97.6744%), Fisher exact p = 2.199086e-14, odds ratio 840. The 2026-09-09 success is the single surviving attach in that whole period. The route DID die, and it died on a date. The pooled 67.1875% is the weaker statement of the two and should not be quoted on its own.
restore: Paste the `entry` object back into `mcpServers` in the config named above, or copy the backup over it, then restart the application.

change_point.cross_checks: chi-square with Yates correction p = 8.709349e-13; mpmath exact hypergeometric tail agreeing with scipy to 2.2e-14

disabled_not_retired: The entry is DISABLED, not retired. He has emailed Wolfram about the MCP licence, which is separate from the desktop Engine licence, and said of the service: 'It has its uses. For example you can talk to it in natural language and get useful output back.' That capability is a named loss: wolframscript takes Wolfram Language, not English. Follow-up is task W1.
